summary: Tested all 6 new HRlytic features: Italian cities seed, succession critical roles fix, WF Alignment KPI rename, Skills Map V2, Internal Mobility, Action Center. Backend pytest: 20/20 passed. Frontend Playwright: all 3 new pages render correctly, sidebar navigation present, Italian cities visible in regression, alert resolve flow works (26 -> 25 after resolve), Turnover filter narrows list to 8 alerts.

minor.issue: no_successor KPI returns 0 — every critical role finds at least one candidate >=55 readiness. Spec wording ('with some having no successors') is not strictly met; data/threshold tuning may be needed if business expects gaps to surface. Risk distribution is well balanced (16/11/17/1).

Action Center returns 4 sources (Turnover, Org Health, Skills, Headcount). The Succession source is implemented but produces 0 alerts because no_successor=0 (see above). UI 'Succession' filter button is therefore non-functional. Sources KPI shows 4 — matches spec.

GET /api/dashboard/skills-map-v2 returns kpis {tracked_skills:47, critical_gaps:6, avg_coverage:82.5, emerging_skills:13}, 27 gaps with suggested_action, heatmap (3 categories × 10 depts), demand_supply top-15

Frontend /internal-mobility renders 58 positions; clicking position loads top-10 matches with fit %, matched skills (green tags w/ proficiency), missing skills, performance & mobility flags

Sidebar contains sidebar-nav-skills-map, sidebar-nav-internal-mobility, sidebar-nav-action-center in correct groupings (Planning/Talent/Insights)
Headcount page renders Genova and Villanova d'Asti in city distribution chart
No console/page errors on any of the 3 new pages
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1786 lines (up from 1485). Strongly recommend splitting into routers: planning_router, insights_router, mobility_router, people_router. Maintenance & test isolation suffering.

_compute_matches in positions endpoint iterates active employees + skill loops, then is called once per position inside /positions for internal_fit KPI calculation (line 1608-1611). For 58 positions × 386 employees this is ~22k iterations on every /positions call. Cache per request or precompute supply once.

Alert resolution is in-memory only (POST /alerts/resolve always returns success but does not persist state). This is acknowledged as MOCKED in problem statement, but the GET /alerts call will re-return resolved alerts on next page load — UI state only. Document this clearly or persist to DB.

Hardcoded random seeds (random.Random(51), random.Random(52)) in /positions and /alerts make KPIs deterministic but disconnected from actual data (filled_internally, resolved_this_month). Acceptable for MVP demo, flag for production.

Succession alert rule (Rule 2 in /alerts) currently produces 0 alerts because readiness threshold is identical to the succession endpoint's threshold — by definition the source can never fire. Either lower the alert threshold (e.g. readiness>=70) or remove the Succession filter button from UI to avoid empty filter UX.
seed_data_creation: Used existing seed (DELETE /api/data/reset was already done by main agent). Verified 386 active employees, 79+36=115 in Italian cities, 45 critical roles for succession.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 22+ backend dashboard endpoints functional. New page testids: skills-map-v2-page, internal-mobility-page, action-center-page. Position cards testid format: position-{uuid}. Alert cards: alert-{id}. Filter buttons: filter-{source-lower}. Resolve buttons: resolve-{id}. Skill gap items: skill-gap-{i}. Match cards: match-{i}. Position IDs are deterministic uuid5 — same across calls. Alert resolve is client-state only (MOCKED). Action Center has 4 working sources; Succession filter exists but currently empty due to no_successor=0 (data tuning issue, not bug).
rca_minor_observations: no_successor=0 root cause: readiness threshold of 55 in both /succession (line 1235) and /alerts Rule 2 (line 1694) is liberal enough that every Band E / talented Band D role finds a Band C/D candidate with >=55 score given current skill overlap distribution. Either tighten threshold (e.g. >=70) or accept current behavior. Not a code bug — design/threshold choice.
